newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks seen weakening further on property fears.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks seen weakening further on property fears.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks are expected to face more selling on Thursday, particularly in the property sector where concerns remain that prices may have peaked.

"I think for the time being investors are still cautious on the property market because prices have gone up too much, so they may continue to reduce weightings in property stocks," said Peter So, deputy head of research at Schroder Securities.
"Yesterday the long bond yield in the U.S. also went up and we may see selling pressure in the banking stocks," he added.
The Hang Seng Index tumbled 133.07 points, or one percent, to 13,119.13 on Wednesday.
Later the Hang Seng London Reference Index of Hong Kong stocks traded in London fell 40.58 points to 13,078.55. Overnight the U.S. long bond fell 11/32 to yield 6.88 percent.
"The market will continue to be dragged down by weakness in the property stocks because of concerns about an interest rate hike," said Dharmala Securities director of research Ben Kwong.
"The market is now trying to establish a bottom," he said.
Kwong said the Hang Seng Index should find support around 12,800. "I think the market will test the lower support first and then rebound," he added.
